//: The DEPLOYED-SITE budget run (BUILD_PROGRESS step 36, item 1).
`lighthouserc.json` collects from `staticDistDir` — the built artifact
served off a local static server. Same bytes, same budgets, every commit.
What it cannot test is everything the CDN is responsible for: whether the
response is actually compressed, whether cache lifetimes are set, which
HTTP version and TLS the edge negotiates. Those contribute to real 4G
field performance as much as the bytes do, and 'the site loads in under 2s
on a throttled 4G mobile profile' is a claim about the SITE.
So this config is not a copy of the local one. The two audits that are
deploy-specific — `uses-text-compression` and `uses-long-cache-ttl` — are
`warn` locally because a static file server cannot satisfy them, and are
ERRORS here, because the edge can and must. Everything else keeps the same
thresholds so a regression means the same thing in both places.
Run after the deploy step in `deploy.yml`, gated on the Cloudflare token
like the post-deploy smoke test, so forks and pull requests never reach a
network check. Two runs rather than three: the local job already samples
three times, and this one is about the edge, not about variance.
The TIMING budgets are `warn` here on purpose, and only the two edge
audits are errors. The local job enforces the same thresholds on the same
bytes over three runs on a loopback server; asserting them again across a
real network from a GitHub runner adds flake, not signal, and this step
runs AFTER the deploy, so a flake would raise a red cross on a release
that is already live. A regression still shows: a warning is reported and
the full Lighthouse report is uploaded. What is an ERROR here is what only
the deploy can get wrong.
Verified against the live site before this landed: `content-encoding: br`
on the document, and `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`
on the hashed assets — so both error-level audits pass today, and a
failure means the edge configuration changed.
